### Subject: Opinion on applicability of Equalisation Levy on payments for online advertisement services to a non-resident platform

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of AdReach Media Private Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. ## 2. Statement of Facts

AdReach Media Private Limited pays annual charges of INR 1.5 crore to a non-resident digital advertising platform, which has no permanent establishment in India, for online advertisement space targeting Indian users.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the payments are subject to Equalisation Levy under Section 165 of the Finance Act, 2016, and at what rate.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 165, Finance Act, 2016
- Section 10(50)


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- CBDT FAQs on Equalisation Levy

## 6. Analysis

As AdReach is a resident carrying on business, the payment does not relate to a permanent establishment of the non-resident in India, and the aggregate annual payment exceeds the INR 1 lakh threshold, the online advertisement services fall within the scope of Section 165, attracting Equalisation Levy at 6%, to be deposited by AdReach on a quarterly basis (separately from, and not deductible from, the amount paid to the non-resident unless contractually grossed up).

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

AdReach Media Private Limited is liable to deduct and deposit Equalisation Levy at 6% on the advertisement payments made to the non-resident platform.

**Confidence level:** High
